requirements: The core contributions of the survey paper 'Recursive Self-Improvement in AI: From Bounded Self-Refinement to Autonomous Research Loops' have been reproduced, including its corpus construction, two-axis taxonomy, category-wise mapping of 1,250 papers, verification hierarchy, and failure-mode analysis.

sub_tasks.requirements: The computational environment, arXiv/OpenAlex query infrastructure, and classification/analysis tooling needed to reproduce the survey are set up.

The Python runtime and package dependencies required for arXiv querying, OpenAlex enrichment, text processing (TF-IDF, SVD), dimensionality reduction (t-SNE), and plotting are installed and importable.

Code has been implemented to establish a Python (>=3.9) environment with a pinned requirements.txt or equivalent listing arxiv, requests (for OpenAlex REST calls), pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, and tqdm.

Code has been implemented so that a smoke-test script imports every required library (arxiv, requests, pandas, numpy, sklearn.feature_extraction.text.TfidfVectorizer, sklearn.decomposition.TruncatedSVD, sklearn.manifold.TSNE, matplotlib) and exits with a zero status.
Code has been implemented to fix random seeds (numpy, sklearn) for reproducible SVD/t-SNE embeddings used in the semantic map.
The arXiv query infrastructure supporting the seven-thread seed harvest and three-direction supplemental harvest is implemented as a reusable module.

Code has been implemented that wraps the arXiv API to issue category- and keyword-scoped queries with a configurable date range (defaulting to 2024-01-01 through 2026-06-30) and returns structured records (arxiv_id, title, abstract, authors, primary_category, submission_date).
Code has been implemented that enforces a configurable per-query result cap (as described in Section 2.3) and paginates the arXiv API safely with retry-on-error and rate-limit backoff.

The query configuration file enumerates exactly seven seed threads (self-refinement, self-rewarding training, automated AI research, self-modifying agents, LLM-driven code/algorithm discovery, RSI theory and safety, self-generated-data loops) and three supplemental directions (self-evaluation methods, test-time training, zero-data self-play), each with an explicit query string.
The OpenAlex enrichment layer that attaches citation counts and venue metadata to harvested arXiv records is implemented.

Code has been implemented to look up each arXiv record in OpenAlex (via DOI or title match) and merge citation count, host venue, and publication year into the record schema, with graceful handling of missing matches.
Code has been implemented so that OpenAlex API calls use polite-pool headers (User-Agent with contact email) and cache responses to a local store to avoid repeated network calls on re-runs.
The classification and analysis tooling that maps papers into the two-axis taxonomy and supports keyword rules plus per-paper overrides is implemented.

Code has been implemented that applies thread-default category assignments followed by keyword rules on title and abstract to reclassify papers into the four technical categories plus foundations family, matching the pipeline described in Section 2.3.
Code has been implemented that supports an explicit per-paper override table (arxiv_id -> category) that takes precedence over keyword rules, enabling the manual corrections described in Section 2.3.
The classification pipeline emits a per-paper assignment log (arxiv_id, thread_default, rule_hit, final_category) so that reclassifications and overrides are auditable, as promised in Section 2.3.
Deterministic behavior of the classification pipeline on the reported override counts is verified.
When run on the seed corpus, the classification pipeline reports that rule-based reclassification moves exactly 89 seed papers off their thread defaults, matching Section 2.3.
The explicit per-paper override table contains exactly 3 entries corresponding to the misfires caught during writing, as stated in Section 2.3.

The 393-paper Deployment-time self-evolution category is surveyed across the six sub-threads (output refinement, code self-repair, multimodal self-critique, test-time training, harness/agent evolution, skill libraries), preserving the paper's persistence-ordered narrative and anchor citations.

The category-level framing (§3 opener and Figure 3) is reproduced: 393 papers, persistence-ordered narrative (refined outputs evaporate, TTT persists per session, harness/skills accumulate), and anchor citations to Self-Refine, Reflexion, and Snell et al.'s inference-time scaling.
Code has been implemented that reports the Deployment-time self-evolution category size as 393 papers and identifies it as the largest of the four technical categories in the corpus.
Code has been implemented reporting that 74% of the Deployment-time self-evolution papers were posted in 2026, matching the corpus statistics in Table 1.

Code has been implemented that renders/describes Figure 3, ordering the six sub-threads on a persistence axis (episode-scoped refinement -> session-scoped TTT -> indefinitely accumulating harness/skill changes).
The opener explicitly cites Self-Refine [6] and Reflexion [17] as the 2023 origin of the generate-critique-revise loop, and Snell et al. [18] for the inference-time scaling-law framing.

Section 3.1 surveys self-critique and self-verification for text and reasoning along three lines (structured/symbolic feedback, search-shaped refinement, and diagnostic critique) with the Huang et al. negative result and 2026 follow-ups.

Code has been implemented covering the structured/symbolic feedback thread, citing SymbolicAI [19], planning-with-symbolic-validators [20], SQL executors [21], clinical hallucination detectors [22], and QA-based factuality probes [23], and stating the design lesson that the refinement loop is only as good as the feedback channel.

The search-shaped refinement line is covered, citing SQL-o1's self-reward heuristic search [21] and LLM-Personalize's reinforced self-training [24], and noting the blur with training-time methods (§4).

The diagnostic study of document-level literary translation [26] is reported as covering nine LLMs and seven language pairs, with the finding that refinement gains concentrate in fluency/style/terminology and project outputs toward the refiner's own distribution.
Huang et al.'s [27] negative result is stated: absent external feedback, LLMs largely cannot self-correct reasoning, and naive self-correction can make answers worse.

The section reports that the 2026 literature responded by grounding critique in external signals and cites the task-sensitive mechanism analysis [28], the four-level calibration study [29], and BinEval's atomic binary-question decomposition [30].
Section 3.2 surveys code self-repair via execution feedback, covering affirmative applications, the decomposition of why feedback helps, and feedback-resolution advances (FLARE, CoSPlay).

The affirmative applications are covered: Blender 3D-asset multi-agent generation [31], database tuning [32], compiler-pass tuning [33], Lean theorem proving via LEAP [34], Rust verification via KVerus [35], specification generation against knowledge bases [36], and verifier-guided decoding [37].

The decomposition literature is covered, citing the student-teacher protocol separating feedback from resampling/format/compute [38], the placebo-controlled Popperian falsification study [39], the small-model topology-vs-feedback result [40], pre-execution structural checks for inter-tool contracts [41], and multi-round repair evaluations [42].

DISC [43] is described as treating verification-question outputs as noisy measurements of where a solution is corrupted, extending the code-repair account to reasoning as inference over error locations.

FLARE [44] is described as a line-level suspiciousness diagnostic between generation and revision, and CoSPlay [45] as co-evolving code and test populations to handle spuriously coupled self-generated tests.

Section 3.3 surveys vision-language and multimodal self-critique, covering hallucination mitigation, generation self-refinement, active perception, safety at the codebook level, and the cautionary VLM-judge/self-play threads.

Kestrel [46] is covered as training-free visually-grounded self-refinement for LVLM hallucinations, Reflect-R1 [47] as the multimodal restatement of Huang et al.'s negative result via evidence-driven external retrieval, unified MLLM self-refinement of text-to-image outputs [48], and Proprio [49] as a proprioceptive latent-space self-scoring signal for physical plausibility.

ActiveScope [50] is described as diagnosing contextual dominance and semantic bias and actively re-examining regions, and the iteratively self-improving codebook work [51] is described as purging unsafe visual patterns from the autoregressive image-generator token vocabulary.

The cautionary threads are covered: the self-evolving LMM study [52] showing self-play/self-consistency optimizes answer agreement while under-attending to visual content (visual under-conditioning), personal visual context grounding [53], and JudgeFit [54] discovering per-judge internal taxonomies of physical phenomena before trusting scores.

The §3.1-3.3 assessment is included, stating that inference-time refinement is bounded self-improvement whose improvements evaporate at episode end, that the half-life problem motivates §4 and §3.5-3.6, and that the field's design rule is 'no external signal, no reliable improvement'.
Section 3.4 surveys test-time training as the middle regime between frozen-weight refinement and offline training.

The three TTT mechanisms are covered: query-conditioned test-time self-training [55], continual variants converting inference-time reasoning traces into persistent lightweight memories [56], and consolidation via a periodic 'sleep' phase [57].

Code has been implemented reporting that the supplemental harvest finds 87 papers in the test-time-training thread and positioning TTT as astride the §3/§4 boundary (training persistence with per-query granularity).

Section 3.5 surveys harness and agent self-evolution, from the conceptual poles (Gödel Agent, Darwin Gödel Machine, metacognitive learning) through what actually gets evolved (prompts, verifiers, evaluators, topology, data, infrastructure) to measurement and sobriety about returns.

The conceptual poles are covered: the Gödel Agent [9] (named for Schmidhuber [2]) as self-referential runtime-code rewriter searching the full agent-design space, the Darwin Gödel Machine [10] as empirical-benefit relaxation with an open-ended archive validated on coding benchmarks, and Liu et al.'s [58] intrinsic-metacognitive-learning argument.

The 'what actually gets evolved' inventory is covered across levels: prompt-level environment-feedback optimization [59], verification-level rubric/verifier evolution in deep-research agents [60], Red Queen co-evolution of agents with evaluators [61], Escher-Loop's self-referential optimizer-agents against a dynamic benchmark [62], topology-level multi-agent structure evolution [63], data-level verifiable-trajectory generation for computer-use agents [64], and experience-graph infrastructure [65].

The practitioner-facing coding-agents analysis [14] is cited for the cultural shift that the engineered artifact is now the loop (trigger, goal, verification, stopping rule, memory) rather than the step-by-step prompt.

The Meta-Agent Challenge [66] is described as the first benchmark for autonomous agent-system development given a sandbox, evaluation API, and time budget, and SAGE [67] as comparing isolated vs. socialized evolution under matched compute.
Code has been implemented reporting the systematic Pareto analysis [68] as covering 34 inference-scaling configurations across self-consistency, self-refinement, debate, and mixture-of-agents.

Code has been implemented reporting the peak inference-scaling gain of +7.1 points over chain-of-thought at roughly 20× compute budget from [68], with the observation that self-consistency saturates early while multi-agent gains persist.

Section 3.6 surveys skill libraries and persistent accumulation from Voyager onward, including SkillsBench's negative result, the skill-writing research program, federation/co-evolution/constraint patterns, and the safety literature.

Voyager [69] is cited as introducing the ever-growing library of reusable, composable skills distilled from experience and paired as natural-language procedures with executable code loaded at runtime.
Code has been implemented reporting that on SkillsBench human-authored skills improve pass rates by 16.2 points [70].
Code has been implemented reporting that on SkillsBench LLM-authored skills provide no measurable pass-rate gain [70], framing the sub-thread as a research program to close that gap.

The skill-writing research program is covered: SkillAxe's evaluation-guided self-refinement [70], Skill-R1's recurrent RL decoupled from a closed-source task model [71], SkillRevise's trace-conditioned cold-start revision [72], AlgoSkill's human-like scheduling for algorithm design [73], and SkillMaster's internalization of create/refine/select [74].
Cross-user skill federation without sharing raw trajectories [75], skill/tool co-evolution [76], and execution-trace-derived weakness-targeted training tasks for coding agents [77] are covered.

SHARP [78] is described as evolving a human-auditable rubric policy for financial trading agents, arguing that in low signal-to-noise environments unbounded prompt evolution cannot distinguish logic flaws from market variance, and generalizing the pattern of constraining the self-modification surface for verifiability.

The safety literature is covered: SkillMutator's cross-modal spec/code mismatch attacks [79], SkillHarness for continual skill learning in adversarial environments [80], VASO's formally verifiable skill evolution for physical agents [81], the threat analysis identifying permanently encoded self-amplifying transmissible adversarial influence [82], and 'healthy evolution' work on capability degradation and safety drift without an adversary [83].

The section-3.6 assessment is included, stating that harness/skill evolution is where bounded self-refinement shades into open-ended self-modification, that autonomy is modest (one sandboxed component per system, DGM's empirical validation as SOTA), and that persistence changes the risk calculus (accumulation-without-verification as the core problem).

The 340-paper Training-time self-iteration category (Section 4) is surveyed across the five paradigms (self-rewarding RL, CoT self-training, on-policy self-distillation, self-play including zero-data, embodied/synthetic-data loops), with the four failure modes (rise-and-collapse, scientific amnesia, style drift, prefix failure) and Figure 4 documented.
The Section 4 corpus scope and structural framing are reproduced.

Code has been implemented that filters the 1,250-paper corpus to the Training-time self-iteration category and produces a per-paradigm assignment (self-rewarding RL, CoT self-training, on-policy self-distillation, self-play, embodied/synthetic-data loops) with an executable manifest.
The Training-time self-iteration category contains 340 papers in the reproduced corpus assignment (measured, matches Table 1).
The share of Training-time self-iteration papers posted in 2026 is 69% in the reproduced statistics (measured, matches Table 1).
Code has been implemented that renders Figure 4 as a training-time self-iteration loop diagram covering the five paradigms of §4 with the failure modes attached to the evaluate-and-select station.

The section explicitly anchors the training-time lineage to STaR, ReST^EM, SPIN, and Self-Rewarding Language Models as the four historical anchors preceding the 2024-2026 wave, with citations resolved.
Self-rewarding RL sub-thread (§4.1) is surveyed with its anchor works, the verifier-gating argument, and the rise-and-collapse and scientific-amnesia failure modes.

The §4.1 write-up covers ReST-MCTS* (process-reward tree search vs. final-answer filtering), SEVA (verification as an agent emitting evidence alignments and calibrated confidence), EvoIdeator (checklist-grounded rewards for scientific ideation), and RePro (retrospective progress-awareness) as the process-reward diversification.
The section discusses the interpretability finding that language models encode a 'value axis' in activation space tracking whether the current trajectory is on track, as raw material for self-reward.

Self-Trained Verification is presented as the category's endgame framing, explicitly stating that test-time verification-refinement and training-time self-training are gated by the same verifier bottleneck, with the open question of whether verifier self-training escapes or relocates circularity flagged.

The rise-and-collapse failure mode is documented: Lin's REINFORCE post-training study shows pass@1 climbing and then collapsing within the same run (sometimes to near zero) under a verifiable binary reward, and KL/EWC-style constraints do not prevent it.

The scientific-amnesia failure mode is documented: repeated DPO training across preference campaigns preserves learned behaviors but fails to accumulate methodological knowledge about running the next campaign.
LLM-generated reward-design failures (reward flooding, semantic misunderstanding of the environment API) are surveyed as motivating iterative-debugging framing rather than one-shot generation.
CoT self-training sub-thread (§4.2) is surveyed with the STaR backbone, verifier-free variants, and the three 2026 correctives (efficiency, joint optimization, scope limits).

The §4.2 write-up presents STaR as the backbone recipe (sample rationales, keep correct-answer ones, fine-tune, repeat) and covers Re-ReST (reflector repairing failed trajectories with environment feedback), PRefLexOR (recursive preference optimization over intermediate steps), and LaTRO (latent-variable objective with no external reward).
The elicitation-vs-creation framing is documented: post-training amplifies latent capability rather than creating it, with references to the 2026 boundary-condition mapping literature.

Verifier-free variants Self-Verified Distillation (unlabeled questions, no ground truth/tools/teacher, prompt-based self-verification filtering) and Semi-CoT (semi-supervised pseudo reasoning supervision) are covered.

The efficiency corrective is discussed: o1-style long thinking overshoots on trivial problems, incorrect traces exhibit more unproductive self-reflection than correct ones at matched length, motivating segment-level credit assignment.
The joint-optimization corrective is discussed with ThinkTwice interleaving solving and refining under the same binary reward to make self-refinement a trained capability.

The scope-limits corrective is documented via the negative result that 'a verifiable search is not a learnable chain-of-thought' — an identifiable class of procedures models can execute but cannot internalize via fine-tuning.
On-policy self-distillation sub-thread (§4.3) is surveyed with the paradigm definition, theoretical unification, and the style-drift and prefix-failure structural pathologies.

The §4.3 write-up defines the OPSD recipe as a single model acting as student and privileged teacher (same weights with extra information: reference solution, verified feedback, richer context) with dense token-level supervision, no external teacher, no reward model.
The write-up notes OPSD is the youngest thread (did not exist before 2026) and identifies it as the most closed training loop in routine use, referencing the dedicated survey.
The power-distribution theoretical unification is cited as unifying sampling, self-reward RL, and self-distillation as instances of one distributional operation.

The empirical refinements are surveyed: negative rollouts carry more information than positive ones and should be reweighted, unmanaged difficulty routing over-optimizes easy problems, procedural information can be retained as distilled memory across episodes.
Purified OPSD is cited as showing the vanilla recipe consistently fails on long-CoT reasoning models, destabilizing the reflective behaviors it is meant to strengthen.

The style-drift failure mode is documented: contrastive analysis shows the privileged-vs-unprivileged learning signal concentrates on style tokens rather than task-bearing ones (the hinted teacher writes shorter, more direct text), producing 'privilege-induced style drift' that destabilizes training or collapses response length.

The prefix-failure structural pathology is documented: dense per-token supervision induces a bimodal teacher mixture with fragmented gradients that no token-level loss reweighting can repair, forcing intervention at the trajectory level.
